report.title: Thirteen days in: the governance machine is built, the product is still one module — and the gate is red.
report.subject: Pediatric CDS Platform
report.scope_note: Nine work programs have merged in thirteen days. What they built is almost entirely the evidence-and-governance substrate: a deterministic rf-bundle converter with a fail-closed emission gate, a git-signed clinical review workflow, a rights ledger, five schema-forced release gates, and ten ADRs. What a clinician can actually open in a browser is still the single anemia module it was on day one. Two things now stand between the program and forward motion: `npm run check` is red on `main` from eight failures that predate every open branch and need owner adjudication, and every path from verified evidence to a grounded rule terminates at a named credentialed human who has not been recruited. This report separates what shipped, what a machine can still do, and what only a person can — with a copyable handoff on every open item.
report.constraints: UNVALIDATED RESEARCH PROTOTYPE — automated checks prove software behavior, never clinical validity, safety, or regulatory status. Never populate approvedBy[]/clinicalApprovers[] and never add a `synthetic: false` reviewer-roster entry. No generative model in the clinical decision path. No invented thresholds; missingness is never treated as normal. FIRST_PARTY_BINARY_ALLOWLIST and QUOTED_RUN_ALLOWLIST may only shrink — a new entry is an escalation, not an edit. `npm run check` must be green before commit; it is currently RED on main (8 of 2,786 tests).

items.title: Adjudicate the 6 stale pinned baselines blocking the check gate
items.note: Test IDs 336, 789, 814, 2132, 2133, 2138 all compare live files against literals pinned by a prior phase. Example: tests/ef-p4-t8-honesty-ac.test.mjs pins modules/anemia/module.json at sha256:57280d04… while the live file hashes sha256:334ad705… (it last changed legitimately in PR #20). Each needs a per-item call: legitimate drift → re-pin with recorded rationale, or real regression → fix the data. A prior delegate naively regenerated the p4-t1-pre-merge-snapshot fixture, which made the guarantee compare current state against itself — vacuously true — and added a failure. That was reverted; do not repeat it.

handoff.prompt: Read MBF-1 Cluster B in the findings doc. For each of the 6 failing pinned-baseline tests, determine from git history whether the drift is a legitimate prior-phase change (re-pin, recording the commit that justified it) or a real regression (fix the data). Never regenerate a whole snapshot fixture — that makes the guarantee self-comparing. Present per-item recommendations before editing.

items.title: Decide D-1 and D-2 — the two rights-honesty D1 invariant failures
items.note: Test 2363: FIRST_PARTY_BINARY_ALLOWLIST rejects 11 first-party binaries committed by PR #29 (8 .jpg visual-evidence screenshots, 3 .png mockups). The allowlist's own contract states it MAY ONLY SHRINK and that a new entry is 'the exact failure mode D1 exists to prevent — an escalation, not an edit.' Test 2364: two capture surfaces carry an 8-word quoted run against a 7-word budget (modules/anemia/evidence-assertions.json assertions[10].applicability.ageRange and modules/kidney_suite_v1 assertions[31]). Rewording a capture body is source-expression-adjacent content work. No agent may resolve either without an explicit owner ruling.

handoff.prompt: Owner decision, no agent path. D-1: allowlist, relocate, or narrow scope for the 11 PR-#29 first-party binaries. D-2: reword the two over-budget ageRange quoted runs to 7 words, or allowlist them. Both allowlists are declared shrink-only — widening either is a deliberate, reviewable governance act, never a build fix.

items.title: Launch RF-ANE-001 — the anemia red-cell indices evidence run
items.note: Triggered by real user feedback: the assessment accepts hemoglobin but not hematocrit. The gap is structural — Hct appears in no schema, no rule, no reference range, and `additionalProperties: false` makes POST /api/v1/assess reject the key outright. Because hemoglobin is required, a clinician working from a report that leads with a spun crit cannot run the tool at all. Investigating it surfaced five more instances of the same class: wherever the KB lacks a sourced pediatric numeric interval for a red-cell index, the engine substitutes a clinician-entered dropdown. The run produces the evidence substrate that would make adding a field legitimate; it does not add the field. Note the working tree carries an uncommitted status flip on this doc (design-ready-not-launched → approved).

handoff.prompt: Launch the three legs in doc 06: an rf deepen run extending the RF-EV-001 bundle, the three owner-run DR HITL packets, and the numerics hunt for threshold-carrying independently-retrievable passages. Check the rf catalog first (GET $RF_API_URL/api/catalog/search) — a verified claim may already exist. rf stops at verified claims; it authors no rule and writes no attestation.

items.title: Finish the three-module evidence run (CBC · Growth · Kidney)
items.status_label: 1 of 12 DR packets returned · rf legs unlaunched
items.note: Doc 05 is a launch-ready design; 12 DR HITL packets (4 modules × 3 providers) are authored and committed. One has been run: the CBC ChatGPT Deep Research packet returned 27 net-new candidate rows with open-access numeric anchors (CALIPER 2020 age-banded WBC/ALC/AMC/MCV, pediatric ITP platelet action bands, ASH leukocytosis thresholds, severe aplastic anemia criteria) — correctly self-labelled `inference` where a row derives from a reference-interval boundary rather than a source-stated cutoff. That output is sitting untracked in the working tree at dr-packets/cbc/chatgpt-dr/expected-output/rf-cbc-002-gpt-dr.md and is not committed. No rf deepen run has been launched for any of the three modules.

handoff.prompt: First commit the untracked CBC ChatGPT DR output so the returned research is tracked. Then import it into rf as a candidate feeder only — platform_synthesis never launders into verified evidence — and launch the rf deepen legs for cbc_suite_v1, growth_suite_v1 and kidney_suite_v1 per doc 05 §2. Only verified bundles are admitted; speculation and unsupported claims are rejected outright.

items.title: Approve growth and kidney authoring decisions so the converter can emit rules
items.status_label: human review act · 0 of 4 approved each
items.note: This is DF-E1-M1, and it is not the missing-file problem doc 05 described. All four modules now carry a committed authoring-decisions.yaml. The converter's emission gate is coded as an allowlist — `status === 'approved_for_rule_draft'` is the ONLY permitting condition (propose.mjs:286). growth_suite_v1 and kidney_suite_v1 each hold 4 decisions at `drafted_pending_human_approval`, a deliberately non-approving scaffold status; cbc_suite_v1 holds 4 of 4 approved (hence its 4 rules), anemia 1 of 5. Every review.* field across all four files is `pending` — no named clinical reviewer has evaluated any of it. Flipping a decision to approved is a human act by design; no agent may do it.

handoff.tracker: node_01KXRTYG9GN2KEF45QN6FBW6N5 — EF-WP2 E1 operate: live discovery + council + dual clinical review
handoff.prompt: Human review act, no agent path. A qualified reviewer reads each drafted decision against its cited rf claim and exact assertion, then flips status to approved_for_rule_draft where the reasoning holds. That status means ready-to-draft, not clinical sign-off — the review.* fields track sign-off separately and additionally require G1.

items.title: Ground the first rules — bind rules to attested source passages
items.status_label: 0 of 95 rules · ledger empty by design
items.note: evidence-packs/passage-attestations.json ships with rules[] and candidates[] both empty. Measured from code, the gap is roughly two-thirds attestation-shaped — 60 rules whose sentinel's primary source already has at least one bindable passage, blocked only by the empty ledger — and one-third licensing-shaped: 31 rules bound to AAP2026_IDA, whose 7 passages are quarantined source-not-independently-retrievable. 13 passages are bindable today (BLOOD 5, WHO 3, CDC 2, BSH 2, FDA 1) and none has been bound. The catch: those 13 survivors are the numerics-light paraphrases — the threshold-bearing passages were quarantined for omits-source-numerics — so attesting them grounds rules to thin framework claims rather than to the cutoffs those rules actually encode. Binding requires a named credentialed clinician attesting each rule individually.

handoff.prompt: Human-only. Recruit and out-of-band verify a named credentialed clinician (G1), then have them attest rules individually against the 13 currently-bindable passages. Expect thin coverage: the bindable survivors are numerics-light, so most threshold-bearing rules stay ungrounded until the licensing-shaped 31 are resolved separately. No agent writes an attestation record.

items.title: Ratify the ten ADRs (G0)
items.note: ADR-0001 through ADR-0010, every one still `proposed`. Each clears G0 on its own — partial ratification is real, not a bundle. Until an individual ADR clears, its design stays a recommendation and no downstream artifact may describe it as adopted policy. The software implementing each recommended default already ships, deliberately, so it exists the moment ratification happens — but every real instance stays inert via G1/G2/G3's own schema-forced mechanisms. No task and no script in this repo may write `status: accepted` into an ADR.

handoff.prompt: Human-only, per ADR. Each named decider reads their ADR and records an explicit, attributable ratification in the ADR file itself — not in a session note or commit message. Ratify individually; do not batch. A premature flip does not unblock anything: G1/G2/G3 remain independently schema-enforced.

items.title: Clear the release chain — reviewer roster, signing custodian, data boundary, release authorizer
items.note: G1: governance/reviewer-roster.yaml holds 0 real entries and 5 synthetic dry-run personas; schemas/reviewer-roster.schema.json requires verificationRef whenever synthetic is false, so a real entry is structurally impossible until a credential is verified out-of-band. G2: the release-manifest signature slot is const null on every real candidate — a signing custodian must hold an offline Ed25519 key, and must be a role distinct from the release author. G3: the retrospective harness structurally rejects any fixture lacking a synthetic/de-identified provenance marker; clearing G3 does not by itself flip that off. G4: module.json approvedBy is maxItems: 0 across all four modules, making the unsigned-stub → release-ready transition schema-impossible. Raising any of these ceilings to make a build pass is a defect, never a feature.

handoff.tracker: node_01KXRTYN5FS7F97W5WS45246WG — XC-1 Clinical advisory board + content-governance SOP
handoff.prompt: Human-only, four independent gates. Recruit two clinical reviewers, a laboratory reviewer, an adjudicator and a release authorizer; verify each credential out-of-band and commit the roster entry with verificationRef populated. Separately name a signing custodian and run an offline key ceremony. Never populate approvedBy[] or clinicalApprovers[] to make anything pass.

items.title: Unblock the ARC qualifying clinical-council pilot
items.note: The ARC pediatric clinical council is repository-complete and Portal-authorable (adoption phases P0–P7 all closed out), with a completed synthetic readiness audit that is explicitly non-qualifying. The Phase 5 qualifying-pilot attempt is blocked on two independent owner-held gates: an SDK credential and evidence-rights receipts. An Opus validator reproduced both blocks read-only. Treating any ARC output as credentialed clinical sign-off is one of the two mistakes this program is most likely to make — clinicalApprovers[] and approvedBy[] need real named humans, never ARC output.

handoff.prompt: Owner action only. The arc-runtime-owner provisions an SDK credential and registers evidence-rights receipts, then the qualifying pilot can run. Route the request through doc 03, the single maintained entry point — it owns the pinned baseline, the scaffold/populate/validate/read-verdict workflow, and the rollback runbook. Do not invoke the council ad hoc from another doc.

items.title: Complete the REG-001 and REG-004 legal reviews
items.note: Both are verified as rf evidence bundles — REG-001 the intended-use / non-device-CDS mapping memo, REG-004 the HIPAA / server-PHI controls scoping. Neither has had the actual legal review a qualified professional must perform; both remain not_executed_owner_held per rf-handoff/RESULTS.md. REG-004 gates P3, which is the first phase that touches server/PHI mode. Verified from the RESULTS.md record rather than by re-reading the run trees.

handoff.tracker: node_01KXRTYJWWGM2YJMARF942MTBA — REG-001 Intended-use / non-device-CDS mapping memo
handoff.prompt: Owner action: route both verified rf bundles to qualified counsel. REG-001 covers intended-use and non-device-CDS positioning; REG-004 covers HIPAA controls for the server/PHI mode that P3 introduces. An rf bundle is research input to that review, never a substitute for it.

items.title: Plan and build the CBC Suite (P2) — the product thesis
items.note: Anemia is the wedge; the CBC/cytopenia suite is the product. P2-WP1 through WP6 plus WP9 cover neutropenia, leukocytosis/lymphocytosis + eosinophilia, platelets, pancytopenia, smear integration, a shared severity/urgency + missing-data gate, and referral-readiness output. Nothing is started. The only CBC content that exists is E0's 4-rule cbc_suite_v1 vertical slice. Its evidence input is real — RF-CBC-001/002 are verified and the ChatGPT DR pass returned 27 more candidate rows — but the sequencing rule is structure before safety before content, and both P0 and P1 are done, so P2 is genuinely unblocked on engineering. It is gated on release, not on build.

handoff.prompt: Scope P2-WP1 (neutropenia branch) and P2-WP6 (shared CBC severity/urgency + missing-data gate) as the first slice. Every rule must trace to a verified rf claim through an approved authoring decision — no hand-authored clinical logic, no invented thresholds. Route the candidate rule set through the ARC council per doc 03 before merging any rf-derived proposal.

items.title: Longitudinal workspace + SMART-on-FHIR (P3)
items.note: This is the monetizable layer — longitudinal state, unresolved-abnormality work queue, referral-readiness packets, SMART App Launch, CDS Hooks, FHIR mapping. It is also the phase that triggers server/PHI mode and therefore HIPAA controls, which is why REG-004's legal review gates it. Six work packages, none started. Deferring is correct: the critical path is P0 → P1 → P2 → P3, and P2 has not begun.

handoff.trigger: P2 CBC Suite reaches a merged, council-reviewed rule set AND REG-004's legal review returns a HIPAA controls verdict.
handoff.prompt: Scope the longitudinal state model and SMART App Launch. This is the first surface that leaves the browser-local invariant — the public microsite must keep sending no patient data anywhere, so server/PHI mode is a separate, HIPAA-controlled deployment, never a mode toggle on the public build.
